gitCommit.subject: Show the statement and AI limits, and explain hitting the cap
gitCommit.body:
Show the statement and AI limits, and explain hitting the cap

The trial only ever said how many days were left. Nothing in the app
mentioned that it also caps statement files and AI messages, so a user on an
extended trial had no way to know why an upload was refused in September
when their trial ran to December.

Hitting the cap returns SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED with reason
upload_limit_reached, and the upload modal branched on the code alone: it
closed itself and pushed /premium with no explanation. It now shows the
server's message — which carries the real number — and a Ver Premium action,
since retrying a limit error only fails again.

Adds the used/limit line to the statement files header, reading the numbers
the API reports rather than a constant, because the cap is a server-side env
variable. On the premium screen statement files show as a count, where the
individual number is the point, and AI messages stay a percentage. The
paywall names the cap premium lifts; it says AI messages are expanded rather
than unlimited, because premium raises that budget rather than removing it.

Fixes the counters being stale: they were read from authStore, which is only
written at login and after a plan change, so the premium screen showed the
numbers as of last app launch. Hides "Manage subscription" when there is no
billing_source, so granted-premium users are not sent to a Stripe portal
with no customer behind it. statement_files_limit is now typed nullable, as
the API has always returned null for premium users — that mismatch would
have crashed the usage bar.

Mocks /refresh in the e2e suite. Uploads refresh tokens before sending, so
no upload path was testable at all: every attempt died as a session error
before its request was made.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
